> Status: draft. Check preprocessing and likelihoods for each modality before fitting.

Input: prepared feature-by-sample matrices with matched sample IDs. This
example fits RNA and protein views with Gaussian likelihoods, then inspects
variance, factors, and feature weights.

## 1. Load and match two prepared views

Prepare each modality on its own measurement scale before this step. Do not
convert missing values to zero or apply RNA transformations to another assay.

```{r}
library(MOFA2)
library(qs2)
library(readr)

rna <- qs2::qs_read("input/rna_view.qs2")
protein <- qs2::qs_read("input/protein_view.qs2")
stopifnot(is.matrix(rna), is.matrix(protein))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rownames(rna)), !anyDuplicated(rownames(protein)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(colnames(rna)), !anyDuplicated(colnames(protein)))
stopifnot(all(is.na(rna) | is.finite(rna)), all(is.na(protein) | is.finite(protein)))

samples <- intersect(colnames(rna), colnames(protein))
stopifnot(length(samples) >= 2)
views <- list(
  rna = rna[, samples, drop = FALSE],
  protein = protein[, samples, drop = FALSE]
)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(views$rna), colnames(views$protein)))
```

For another modality, add its matrix to `views` and match its sample order in
the same visible way. MOFA2 can model missing values; this simple example uses
the shared-sample set instead of hidden imputation.

## 2. Configure and fit MOFA2

MOFA is unsupervised. Do not use response labels to select features or tune
the model. The number of factors and likelihoods are model choices.

```{r}
mofa <- MOFA2::create_mofa(views)
data_options <- MOFA2::get_default_data_options(mofa)
data_options$scale_views <- FALSE

model_options <- MOFA2::get_default_model_options(mofa)
model_options$num_factors <- 10
model_options$likelihoods <- c(rna = "gaussian", protein = "gaussian")

training_options <- MOFA2::get_default_training_options(mofa)
training_options$seed <- 1234
training_options$convergence_mode <- "slow"
training_options$maxiter <- 1500

dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
mofa <- MOFA2::prepare_mofa(mofa, data_options = data_options,
                            model_options = model_options,
                            training_options = training_options)
mofa <- MOFA2::run_mofa(mofa, outfile = "output/mofa_model.hdf5",
                        save_data = TRUE, use_basilisk = FALSE)
```

The trained model uses MOFA2's native HDF5 format. Check the current MOFA2
backend instructions if the Python environment cannot be found.

## 3. Check variance explained and factor scores

```{r}
variance <- MOFA2::get_variance_explained(mofa, as.data.frame = TRUE)
print(variance$r2_total)
print(variance$r2_per_factor)
MOFA2::plot_variance_explained(mofa, plot_total = TRUE)

factor_matrix <- MOFA2::get_factors(mofa, groups = "all", factors = "all")[[1]]
factor_scores <- data.frame(sample_id = rownames(factor_matrix), factor_matrix)
boxplot(as.data.frame(factor_matrix), las = 2, ylab = "Factor score")
```

Factor number and sign are not biological identities. A factor that explains
large variance may be technical; review sample quality and processing effects.

## 4. Inspect feature weights

Weights characterize the fitted factors; they do not establish causal genes.

```{r}
weights <- MOFA2::get_weights(mofa, views = "all", factors = "all",
                              scale = FALSE, as.data.frame = TRUE)
head(weights[order(-abs(weights$value)), ], 20)
```

## 5. Test one metadata association (optional)

```{r}
#| eval: false

metadata <- readr::read_tsv("input/sample_metadata.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
metadata <- metadata[match(factor_scores$sample_id, metadata$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(metadata$sample_id, factor_scores$sample_id))
stats::cor.test(metadata$technical_measure, factor_matrix[, "Factor1"],
                method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

Replace `technical_measure` with one numeric QC or processing variable. Apply
multiple-testing correction when assessing several associations.

## 6. Save the model summaries

```{r}
dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_tsv(variance$r2_total, "output/mofa_variance_total.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(variance$r2_per_factor, "output/mofa_variance_by_factor.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(factor_scores, "output/mofa_factor_scores.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(weights, "output/mofa_feature_weights.tsv")
```
